title: Timothy as a Faithful Messenger
speaker: Dr. John Battle

outline.title: The Context of the Mission
subpoints: Paul’s location in Corinth during the second missionary journey
The sudden departure from Thessalonica due to persecution
The separation of Paul, Timothy, and Silas in Athens

outline.title: The Purpose of the Messenger
subpoints: To establish the believers in their faith
To encourage them amidst afflictions and tribulation
To prevent the tempter from shaking their confidence

outline.title: The Qualifications of the Messenger
subpoints: Timothy identified as a brother and minister of God
A fellow laborer in the gospel of Christ
The value of a faithful envoy bringing healing and refreshment

summary:
This morning’s sermon, delivered by Dr. John Battle, examines 1 Thessalonians 3:1-5, focusing on the role of Timothy as a messenger sent by the Apostle Paul to the church in Thessalonica. The message highlights the historical context of Paul’s second missionary journey, specifically the urgent need to support a young church facing intense persecution and instability after Paul’s abrupt departure from the city.

The sermon outlines three key aspects of Timothy’s mission: his purpose, his qualifications, and his message. The purpose was to establish and encourage the believers’ faith, ensuring they would not be shaken by the tempter or the surrounding afflictions. Timothy’s qualifications are described in terms of his relationship to Paul as a brother, minister of God, and fellow laborer, illustrating the importance of faithful service in the church.

Drawing on Proverbs, the sermon emphasizes the spiritual value of a faithful messenger, comparing such a person to cold snow in harvest time, which refreshes the soul. The message serves as a pastoral reminder of the importance of mutual encouragement and the strategic deployment of ministry workers to sustain the faith of the congregation during times of trial.
